items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: Manuel Perez and King Alba would be taking more musicians out of New Orleans than any other people.

ctx.x: Jeanette Sullivan. So we got her to play in the band. And the band made a great success. The band then, I composed a number and we called it My Josephie. And the number made such a hit with the people that it actually swarmed Ridgely's Tuxedo. Really? By the way Ridgely called his band Ridgely's Tuxedo and Celestad called his band Papa Celestad's Tuxedo. But that Ridgely's Tuxedo band died out of the picture. And all that was left was Papa Celestad's Tuxedo band. So I stayed with Papa Celestad band. All that…

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: So he wrote to Manuel and Manuel got to me and then he wrote to me.

ctx.x: Did King Oliver write to you, or did he call you, or what?

King Oliver wrote to me. But he got to me through Manuel Perez. See, Manuel Perez at that time used to send all the best musicians up to the country, with King Oliver. Whenever they'd need something, Manuel Perez would be the man that would send the musicians up there. So he wrote to Manuel and Manuel got to me and then he wrote to me. Had John ever heard you play? He heard me. My recall, he never heard me play at first. I wasn't even playing when he left here. But after he heard that recalling on my Josephine,…

items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: And right down to Manuel Perez and found who it was and Manuel told him who it was.

ctx.x: In the cold weather when they played.

So, in the, up until, I went back with Solis there, last of 25 and I stayed until 27. And by that time King Oliver had heard that record, My Josephine and hearing all the work on the saxophone. And right down to Manuel Perez and found who it was and Manuel told him who it was. And in through Manuel, I went with King Oliver. And that was in 1927.
Where was he when he located you then? He was in Chicago.
